{{Short description|Characterization of surjectivity}}
{{Multiple issues|{{more footnotes|date=May 2020}}{{refimprove|date=May 2020}}}}

The theorem on the '''surjection of Fréchet spaces''' is an important theorem, due to [[Stefan Banach]],{{sfn|Trèves|2006|pp=378-384}} that characterizes when a [[continuous linear operator]] between [[Fréchet spaces]] is [[surjection|surjective]].

The importance of this theorem is related to the [[Open mapping theorem (functional analysis)|open mapping theorem]], which states that a continuous linear surjection between Fréchet spaces is an [[open map]]. Often in practice, one knows that they have a continuous linear map between Fréchet spaces and wishes to show that it is surjective in order to use the open mapping theorem to deduce that it is also an open mapping. This theorem may help reach that goal.

== Preliminaries, definitions, and notation ==
Let <math>L : X \to Y</math> be a continuous linear map between [[topological vector space]]s. 

The [[continuous dual space]] of <math>X</math> is denoted by <math>X^{\prime}.</math>

The [[Transpose of a linear map|transpose]] of <math>L</math> is the map <math>{}^t L : Y^{\prime} \to X^{\prime}</math> defined by <math>L \left(y^{\prime}\right) := y^{\prime} \circ L.</math> If <math>L : X \to Y</math> is surjective then <math>{}^t L : Y^{\prime} \to X^{\prime}</math> will be [[injective]], but the converse is not true in general. 

The [[weak topology]] on <math>X</math> (resp. <math>X^{\prime}</math>) is denoted by <math>\sigma\left(X, X^{\prime}\right)</math> (resp. <math>\sigma\left(X^{\prime}, X\right)</math>). The set <math>X</math> endowed with this topology is denoted by <math>\left(X, \sigma\left(X, X^{\prime}\right)\right).</math> The topology <math>\sigma\left(X, X^{\prime}\right)</math> is the weakest topology on <math>X</math> making all linear functionals in <math>X^{\prime}</math> continuous. 

If <math>S \subseteq Y</math> then the [[Polar set|polar]] of <math>S</math> in <math>Y</math> is denoted by <math>S^{\circ}.</math> 

If <math>p : X \to \R</math> is a [[seminorm]] on <math>X</math>, then <math>X_p</math> will denoted the vector space <math>X</math> endowed with the weakest [[topological vector space|TVS]] topology making <math>p</math> continuous.{{sfn|Trèves|2006|pp=378-384}} A neighborhood basis of <math>X_p</math> at the origin consists of the sets <math>\left\{ x \in X : p(x) < r \right\}</math> as <math>r</math> ranges over the positive reals. If <math>p</math> is not a norm then <math>X_p</math> is not [[Hausdorff space|Hausdorff]] and <math>\ker p := \left\{ x \in X : p(x) = 0 \right\}</math> is a linear subspace of <math>X</math>.  
If <math>p</math> is continuous then the identity map <math>\operatorname{Id} : X \to X_p</math> is continuous so we may identify the continuous dual space <math>X_p^{\prime}</math> of <math>X_p</math> as a subset of <math>X^{\prime}</math> via the transpose of the identity map <math>{}^{t} \operatorname{Id} : X_p^{\prime} \to X^{\prime},</math> which is [[Injective function|injective]].

== Surjection of Fréchet spaces ==

{{math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Trèves|2006|pp=378-384}}|note=Banach|math_statement=If <math>L : X \to Y</math> is  a continuous linear map between two Fréchet spaces, then <math>L : X \to Y</math> is surjective if and only if the following two conditions both hold: 
<ol>
<li><math>{}^t L : Y^{\prime} \to X^{\prime}</math> is [[injective]], and</li>
<li>the [[Image of a function|image]] of <math>{}^t L,</math> denoted by <math>\operatorname{Im} {}^t L,</math> is weakly closed in <math>X^{\prime}</math> (i.e. closed when <math>X^{\prime}</math> is endowed with the weak-* topology). </li>
</ol>
}}

== Extensions of the theorem ==

{{math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Trèves|2006|pp=378-384}}|note=|style=|math_statement=
If <math>L : X \to Y</math> is a continuous linear map between two Fréchet spaces then the following are equivalent:
<ol>
<li><math>L : X \to Y</math> is surjective.
</li>

<li>The following two conditions hold:
<ol style="list-style-type: lower-latin;">
<li><math>{}^t L : Y^{\prime} \to X^{\prime}</math> is [[injective]];</li>
<li>the [[Image of a function|image]] <math>\operatorname{Im} {}^t L</math> of <math>{}^t L</math> is weakly closed in <math>X^{\prime}.</math></li>
</ol>
</li>

<li>For every continuous seminorm <math>p</math> on <math>X</math> there exists a continuous seminorm <math>q</math> on <math>Y</math> such that the following are true:
<ol style="list-style-type: lower-latin;">
<li>for every <math>y \in Y</math> there exists some <math>x \in X</math> such that <math>q(L(x) - y) = 0</math>;</li>
<li>for every <math>y^{\prime} \in Y,</math> if <math>{}^t L\left(y^{\prime}\right) \in X^{\prime}_p</math> then <math>y^{\prime} \in Y^{\prime}_q.</math></li>
</ol>
</li>

<li>For every continuous seminorm <math>p</math> on <math>X</math> there exists a linear subspace <math>N</math> of <math>Y</math> such that the following are true:
<ol style="list-style-type: lower-latin;">
<li>for every <math>y \in Y</math> there exists some <math>x \in X</math> such that <math>L(x) - y \in N</math>;</li>
<li>for every <math>y^{\prime} \in Y^{\prime},</math> if <math>{}^t L \left(y^{\prime}\right) \in X^{\prime}_p</math> then <math>y^{\prime} \in N^{\circ}.</math></li>
</ol>
</li>

<li>There is a [[non-increasing]] sequence <math>N_1 \supseteq N_2 \supseteq N_3 \supseteq \cdots</math> of closed linear subspaces of <math>Y</math> whose intersection is equal to <math>\{ 0 \}</math> and such that the following are true:
<ol style="list-style-type: lower-latin;">
<li>for every <math>y \in Y</math> and every positive integer <math>k</math>, there exists some <math>x \in X</math> such that <math>L(x) - y \in N_k</math>;</li>
<li>for every continuous seminorm <math>p</math> on <math>X</math> there exists an integer <math>k</math> such that any <math>x \in X</math> that satisfies <math>L(x) \in N_k</math> is the limit, in the sense of the seminorm <math>p</math>, of a sequence <math>x_1, x_2, \ldots</math> in elements of <math>X</math> such that <math>L\left(x_i\right) = 0</math> for all <math>i.</math></li>
</ol>
</li>

</ol>
}}

== Lemmas ==
The following lemmas are used to prove the theorems on the surjectivity of Fréchet spaces. They are useful even on their own.

{{math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Trèves|2006|pp=378-384}} |note=|style=|math_statement=
Let <math>X</math> be a Fréchet space and <math>Z</math> be a linear subspace of <math>X^{\prime}.</math> 
The following are equivalent: 
<ol>
<li><math>Z</math> is weakly closed in <math>X^{\prime}</math>;</li>
<li>There exists a basis <math>\mathcal{B}</math> of neighborhoods of the origin of <math>X</math> such that for every <math>B \in \mathcal{B},</math> <math>B^{\circ} \cap Z</math> is weakly closed;</li>
<li>The intersection of <math>Z</math> with every equicontinuous subset <math>E</math> of <math>X^{\prime}</math> is relatively closed in <math>E</math> (where <math>X^{\prime}</math> is given the weak topology induced by <math>X</math> and <math>E</math> is given the subspace topology induced by <math>X^{\prime}</math>).</li>
</ol>
}}

{{math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Trèves|2006|pp=378-384}} |note=|style=|math_statement=
On the dual <math>X^{\prime}</math> of a Fréchet space <math>X</math>, the topology of uniform convergence on compact convex subsets of <math>X</math> is identical to the topology of [[uniform convergence on compact subsets]] of <math>X</math>.
}}

{{math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Trèves|2006|pp=378-384}}|note=|style=|math_statement=
Let <math>L : X \to Y</math> be a linear map between Hausdorff [[locally convex]] TVSs, with <math>X</math> also [[metrizable]]. 
If the map <math>L : \left(X, \sigma\left(X, X^{\prime}\right)\right) \to \left(Y, \sigma\left(Y, Y^{\prime}\right)\right)</math> is continuous then <math>L : X \to Y</math> is continuous (where <math>X</math> and <math>Y</math> carry their original topologies).
}}

== Applications ==

=== Borel's theorem on power series expansions ===

{{math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Trèves|2006|p=390}} |note=E. Borel|style=|math_statement=
Fix a positive integer <math>n</math>. 
If <math>P</math> is an arbitrary [[formal power series]] in <math>n</math> indeterminates with complex coefficients then there exists a <math>\mathcal{C}^{\infty}</math> function <math>f : \R^n \to \Complex</math> whose Taylor expansion at the origin is identical to <math>P</math>.

That is, suppose that for every <math>n</math>-tuple of non-negative integers <math>p = \left(p_1, \ldots, p_n\right)</math> we are given a complex number <math>a_p</math> (with no restrictions). Then there exists a <math>\mathcal{C}^{\infty}</math> function <math>f : \R^n \to \Complex</math> such that <math>a_p = \left(\partial / \partial x\right)^p f \bigg\vert_{x = 0}</math> for every <math>n</math>-tuple <math>p.</math>
}}

=== Linear partial differential operators ===
{{See also|Distribution (mathematics)}}

{{math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Trèves|2006|p=392}}|note=|style=|math_statement=
Let <math>D</math> be a linear partial differential operator with <math>\mathcal{C}^{\infty}</math> coefficients in an open subset <math>U \subseteq \R^n.</math> 
The following are equivalent:
<ol>
<li>For every <math>f \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty}(U)</math> there exists some <math>u \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty}(U)</math> such that <math>D u = f.</math></li>
<li><math>U</math> is <math>D</math>-convex and <math>D</math> is semiglobally solvable.</li>
</ol>
}}

<math>D</math> being {{em|semiglobally solvable in <math>U</math>}} means that for every [[relatively compact]] open subset <math>V</math> of <math>U</math>, the following condition holds: 

:to every <math>f \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty}(U)</math> there is some <math>g \in \mathcal{C}^{\infty}(U)</math> such that <math>D g = f</math> in <math>V</math>. 

<math>U</math> being {{em|<math>D</math>-convex}} means that for every compact subset <math>K \subseteq U</math> and every integer <math>n \geq 0,</math> there is a compact subset <math>C_n</math> of <math>U</math> such that for every [[Distribution (mathematics)|distribution]] <math>d</math> with compact support in <math>U</math>, the following condition holds:

:if <math>{}^{t} D d</math> is of order <math>\leq n</math> and if <math>\operatorname{supp} {}^{t} D d \subseteq K,</math> then <math>\operatorname{supp} d \subseteq C_n.</math>
